question: At which gestational age does the uterine fundus normally reach the level of the umbilicus?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: At 16 weeks the fundus is midway between the pubic symphysis and the umbilicus, not yet at the umbilicus.
Correct. At 20 weeks the fundus reaches the umbilicus. This landmark is important because the SFH in centimetres roughly equals the gestational age in weeks from 20 weeks onward.
By 24 weeks the fundus has risen above the umbilicus. It reaches umbilical level at 20 weeks.
At 28 weeks the fundus is approximately 28 cm above the pubic symphysis — well above the umbilicus.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the uterine growth landmarks: pubic symphysis at 12 weeks, umbilicus at 20 weeks, xiphisternum at 36 weeks.
Correct. 20 weeks = fundus at umbilicus. From 20–34 weeks, SFH (cm) ≈ gestational age (weeks) — a key clinical rule.
